BEFORE THE PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION
                                OF THE STATE OF MISSOURI

        In the Matter of Evergy Metro, Inc. d/b/a               )
        Evergy Missouri Metro’s Request for                     )   File No. ER-2026-0143
        Authority to Implement a General Rate                   )
        Increase for Electric Service                           )

    STAFF’S MOTION TO STRIKE PORTIONS OF EVERGY MISSOURI METRO’S REPLY BRIEF

           COMES NOW the Staff of the Missouri Public Service Commission (“Staff”)

and moves to strike one sentence on Issue 19.B. from the Reply Brief of Evergy Metro, Inc.

d/b/a Evergy Missouri Metro (“EMM”). The sentence misstates what Staff needed to assess

EMM’s asset prioritization methodology and what EMM supplied. In support of this

motion, Staff states as follows:

           1.      Staff moves to strike the following sentence on page 51 of EMM’s Reply Brief:

    “Staff’s concern is access to the historical scoring data, and the Company ﬁled a

    supplemental discovery response with the archived exports that ﬁlled the gaps

    Staff identiﬁed.” 1

           2.      On August 11, 2026, Staff filed the rebuttal testimony of Staff witness

Malachi Bowman. Staff witness Bowman explained that EMM used AssetLens benefit-cost

ratios to select asset replacements and sought to recover their costs. 2

           3.      On September 8, 2026, Staff witnesses Shawn Lange and Malachi Bowman

met with EMM personnel, including Andy Alexander and Rose Wibbenmeyer,



1
    EMM’s Reply Brief, EFIS Item No. 580, p. 51, sentence accompanying n. 352.
2
  Malachi Bowman, Rebuttal Testimony, Exhibit No. 129, EFIS Item No. 478, p. 11, at lines 8–10, and p. 12, at
lines 1–4; EFIS Item No. 153 (ﬁled Aug. 11, 2026).


                                                       1
 on Microsoft Teams to discuss AssetLens. After the meeting, Staff concluded that EMM

could not provide the necessary formulas to Staff due to the conﬁdential nature of

AssetLens. Therefore, retaining the scores would be of little beneﬁt to Staff. 3

           4.       On October 8, 2026, the Commission admitted Staff witness Bowman’s

rebuttal testimony as Exhibit No. 129. 4

           5.       Staff explained in its Initial Post-Hearing Brief, ﬁled November 6, 2026, that it

could not assess EMM’s methodology without the underlying analysis. Staff did not

recommend a disallowance for prior distribution investments, nor did Staff endorse EMM’s

methodology. 5 EMM and Staff ﬁled their reply briefs on November 18, 2026. On Issue 19.B.,

Staff stood on its initial brief. 6

           6.       Paragraph 3(D) of the Commission’s procedural order requires the parties to

cite the portions of the record that support their positions on unresolved issues. 7

Commission rules require evidentiary support for factual assertions in a brief. 8

The Commission controls post-hearing brieﬁng and must base its ﬁndings on competent




3
 The “gap ﬁlled” was that Staff conﬁrmed that EMM retaining these cost beneﬁt scores from AssetLens would
be of little value without understanding how they are calculated.
4
    Malachi Bowman, hearing testimony, Official Transcript, Volume 9, EFIS Item No. 347, p. 71, at lines 4–15.
5
    Staff’s Initial Post-Hearing Brief, EFIS Item No. 354, p. 67.
6
    EMM’s Reply Brief, EFIS Item No. 580, p. 51, n. 352; Staff’s Reply Brief, EFIS Item No. 582, p. 1.
7
 Order Setting Procedural Schedule and Directing the Filing of Dates for Local Public Hearings, EFIS Item
No. 43, p. 6, para. 3(D).
8
 20 CSR 4240-2.080(6)(C), (12). Under subsection (6)(C), counsel certiﬁes after reasonable inquiry that factual
assertions have evidentiary support or speciﬁcally identiﬁes those likely to have support after further
investigation or discovery. Under subsection (12), acceptance for ﬁling does not waive noncompliance.


                                                            2
 and substantial evidence on the whole record. 9 A factual assertion in a brief cannot

substitute for evidence.

            7.       On redirect, Staff witness Bowman testiﬁed that Staff lacked “access to the

    underlying analysis that AssetLens uses to create those beneﬁt cost ratios.” 10

     Staff witness Bowman explained that Staff could not assess whether EMM’s method for

    prioritizing replacements was reasonable “without understanding that underlying

    analysis.” 11

    The record separates what Staff needed from what EMM supplied:

                 •   Staff needed the analysis behind the scores to assess EMM’s methodology.
                     The scores show where AssetLens ranked each project. The scores do not
                     disclose the assumptions and weightings that produced those rankings. 12

                 •   Footnote 352 on page 51 of EMM’s Reply Brief cites page 118 of
                     EMM’s Initial Post-Hearing Brief. Footnote 693 cites EMM witness Alexander’s
                     rebuttal testimony. At page 16, EMM witness Alexander testified that
                     EMM recovered archived scores and filed a supplemental response. 13 EMM
                     witness Alexander also explained that EMM could not share the vendor’s
                     proprietary calculations of individual benefits. 14




9
 Section 386.410.1, RSMo; 20 CSR 4240-2.140(1); 20 CSR 4240-2.120(1); Section 386.410.1 directs the
Commission to prescribe its hearing procedure. Rule 20 CSR 4240-2.140(1) governs brieﬁng. Rule 20 CSR
4240-2.120(1) authorizes the presiding officer to take action necessary to conduct a fair proceeding and
maintain order.
10
     Malachi Bowman, Official Transcript, Volume 9, p. 75, lines 19–25.
11
     Id. at p. 76, lines 5–18.
 Alexander, Rebuttal Testimony, Exhibit No. 1, EFIS Item No. 567, p. 15, at lines 1–7, 13–16; Malachi Bowman,
12

Rebuttal Testimony, p. 13, lines 4–8, through p. 14, lines 1–2.
13
   Alexander, Rebuttal Testimony, p. 16, lines 6–10; EMM’s Initial Post-Hearing Brief, EFIS Item No. 351,
p. 118, n. 693.
14
     Alexander, Rebuttal Testimony, at p. 15, lines 13–16.



                                                             3
            8.       The testimony EMM cites in footnote 352 show that EMM recovered archived

scores and filed a supplemental response. EMM witness Alexander did not testify that the

supplemental response gave Staff the analysis that generated those scores.

           9.       For future investments, Staff witness Bowman proposed comparing EMM’s

investment programs through cost-benefit analyses outside AssetLens. Staff could then

review the assumptions and weightings. 15 The archived scores show results for past lateral

projects. The scores do not compare investment programs, nor do they disclose the

assumptions and weightings Staff witness Bowman proposed for review. 16

           10.      In the final paragraph under Issue 19.B., EMM argues that Staff’s inability to

reproduce a proprietary calculation does not show that the investments lacked value. 17

Staff witness Bowman testiﬁed that Staff could not assess how EMM chose which projects

to pursue without the analysis behind the scores. 18 Staff did not have enough information

to conclude that EMM’s method was unreasonable. Nor could Staff conclude that

the method was reasonable without knowing how AssetLens weighted the factors that went

into the scores.

           11.      EMM’s reference to the supplemental response does not satisfy

paragraph 3(D) of the procedural order. EMM’s witness said the company ﬁled a response,

but did not say the response supplied the missing analysis. Staff recommends that the

Commission strike the sentence quoted in paragraph 1 rather than decide Issue 19.B. on the


15
     Malachi Bowman, Rebuttal Testimony, p. 13, lines 3–8, through p. 14, lines 1–2.
16
     Alexander, Rebuttal Testimony, p. 16, lines 6–10.
17
     EMM’s Reply Brief, p. 51, ﬁnal paragraph under Issue 19.B.
18
     Malachi Bowman, Official Transcript, Vol. 9, p. 76, lines 5–18.



                                                          4
 mistaken premise that Staff received that analysis. If the Commission leaves the sentence

in the brief, Staff recommends that the Commission expressly disregard it, as the

Commission did with references to material outside the record in Evergy Missouri West. 19

           WHEREFORE, Staff respectfully requests that the Commission strike or expressly

disregard the following sentence on page 51 of EMM’s Reply Brief: “Staff’s concern is access

to the historical scoring data, and the Company filed a supplemental discovery response

with the archived exports that filled the gaps Staff identified.” 20

                                                            Respectfully submitted,
